summary: The Swiss Federal Criminal Court convicted former HSBC IT employee Hervé Falciani in his absence of aggravated economic espionage over the leaked client data ('HSBC files') and sentenced him to five years; he was acquitted of the other charges and lived in France, out of reach of extradition. No reward.

target: Bank Julius Bär & Co. AG / Julius Baer Bank & Trust Company Ltd. (Cayman Islands)
summary: Rudolf Elmer, former chief accountant of Julius Bär's Cayman Islands subsidiary, was prosecuted in Zurich for leaking client data to tax authorities, media and WikiLeaks. Zurich courts convicted him in 2011 and 2015 (suspended day-fines); in 2016 the Zurich High Court acquitted him of bank-secrecy offences but gave him a suspended 14-month sentence for threats and forgery, with 220 days already served in pre-trial detention. The Federal Supreme Court upheld the bank-secrecy acquittal in 2018. No reward.
quote: fällte sie eine Freiheitsstrafe von 14 Monaten, wovon 220 Tage durch Untersuchungshaft erstanden seien.
notes: The judgment is anonymised ('X.'); Elmer went public himself and is named for this ruling by law.ch (che-lawch-elmer-2018). Earlier sentences in the same judgment: 240 day-fines of CHF 30 (2011) and 300 day-fines of CHF 150 (2015), both suspended.

summary: LuxLeaks: Antoine Deltour, the former PwC auditor who took the tax rulings, was convicted in 2016 (12-month suspended sentence and EUR 1,500 fine). On 11 January 2018 Luxembourg's Court of Cassation quashed his conviction on whistleblower grounds, and in May 2018 the Court of Appeal acquitted him of the offences linked to the documents given to the journalist. He was never before the ECHR: the 2023 Grand Chamber case was Halet's. No reward.
quote: A.D. was sentenced to a twelve-month prison term, suspended in its entirety, and to a fine of EUR 1,500.
notes: The judgment calls him 'A.D.'; he went public himself and is named by Paperjam (lux-paperjam-halet-2023: 'Deltour was then recognised as a whistleblower by the Court of Cassation'). Correction to the brief: the 2023 ECHR acquittal-type ruling concerned Halet, not Deltour. A remaining conviction over internal training documents ended with the sentence suspended (para 48).

summary: LuxLeaks: Raphaël Halet, a former PwC employee who passed tax returns to a journalist, was convicted in Luxembourg (fine of EUR 1,000 after appeal). The ECHR Grand Chamber held 12 votes to 5 that the conviction violated freedom of expression and awarded him EUR 15,000 for non-pecuniary damage and EUR 40,000 in costs. No reward.
quote: Holds, by twelve votes to five, that there has been a violation of Article 10
notes: Damages, not a reward. Halet is named in the judgment.

summary: Dr Clarissa Zafirov's 2019 qui tam suit alleged false Medicare diagnosis codes. In 2024 the district court dismissed it, holding qui tam relators are unappointed officers in breach of the Appointments Clause. On 1 September 2026 the Eleventh Circuit vacated that ruling and remanded for the remaining constitutional arguments.
quote: we vacate the district court’s order dismissing this case and remand for the district court to evaluate the defendants’ remaining constitutional arguments.
notes: Case remains pending on Take Care and Vesting Clause arguments.
